parsedBrief.product_description: Formula E Gen3/Gen3 Evo Front Powertrain Kit (FPK): a unitised front MGU with integrated SiC inverter, single-speed reduction and differential, packaged to the Spark front-axle bay. Spec common kit (Lucid/Atieva lineage) for regen on Gen3 and limited AWD traction windows on Gen3 Evo.
parsedBrief.mission_statement: Deliver a homologated, bay-constrained front powertrain cassette that meets FIA Gen3/Gen3 Evo front regen and hardware power class within the sealed front-axle envelope for all Formula E teams.
parsedBrief.target_customers: FIA Formula E championship teams and the series spec-supply chain (front powertrain as common kit).
parsedBrief.why_now: Gen3 front is regen-only and Gen3 Evo adds limited AWD traction windows; series needs a single unitised FPK that fits the fixed Spark front bay and meets published electrical/mechanical caps.

metrics.note: DEC-009 freezes architecture at 24,000 rpm; original brief assumption 19,500 superseded

target_material.value: Cast/machined aluminium-alloy structural housing and coolant jackets; thin-gauge electrical-steel stator/rotor laminations; copper wave windings and solid phase busbars with high-temp insulation; high-temperature rare-earth permanent magnets (NdFeB/SmCo class); case-hardened alloy-steel gears, differential, shafts and bearings; SiC power modules on electrically insulating ceramic substrates (AlN/Si3N4 class); aluminium or copper heat spreaders; dielectric cooling oil and water-glycol external coolant; FKM/PTFE or elastomer seals; polymeric electrical insulation. Exact alloy, magnet and insulation grades require supplier qualification.; product: Front Powertrain Kit (MGU + SiC inverter + single-speed reduction + differential as one sealed cassette) supplied identically to all Formula E teams; outputs are recovered HV DC power and bidirectional halfshaft torque

safety_standards.standard: FIA Formula E Technical Regulations (Gen3 / Gen3 Evo powertrain and electrical safety)
Safety requirements for power electronic converter systems and equipment
Electrically propelled road vehicles — Electrical safety specifications for voltage class B electric circuits
Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP Code)

additional_constraints.description: Morphology forced by front-axle bay: wishbone/upright/steering clearance, crash structure/nose box, halfshaft exit height and track, cooling/HV/LV routing corridors, ground clearance and aero floor.

Unitised sealed cassette: concentric stack L1 SiC MCU on upper shelf, L2 outer stator (wave-wound, end-winding microjet oil cooling), L3 hollow PM rotor, L4 planetary + mini-diff inside rotor cavity; halfshaft exits ±X (car-lateral).
Liquid-cooled PMSM class with integrated SiC inverter/MCU in same housing; solid phase busbars stator feed (no long HV AC cables).

Gen3 front role is regen/energy recovery only (no traction); Gen3 Evo adds limited AWD traction windows (starts/Attack Mode/qualifying). Front regen electrical cap pairs with ≤350 kW rear for ≤600 kW total regen.
Cooling, HV DC, and control interfaces must face corridors available in the front bay; no exterior apron larger than bay box.
Spec/common kit for all teams (Lucid/Atieva supplier lineage), not manufacturer-free like the rear MGU.
No public STEP/CAD; proprietary Lucid road-car EDU CAD/silhouette must not be mesh-pasted — press imagery is training check only.

derived_requirements.basis: SVPWM: V_LL,rms ≈ 600/√2 ≈ 424 V; I ≈ 350000/(√3 × 424 × pf 0.95 × η_inv 0.98) ≈ 520 A rms. Sizes SiC modules, solid phase busbars into the stator, and slot copper. Companion expansion used ~550 A rms with more conservative pf/η; not averaged.

derived_requirements.label: Gross winding temperature headroom above coolant inlet
derived_requirements.basis: 180 °C winding limit − 60 °C stated coolant inlet = 120 K total gross headroom (coolant rise, case-to-coolant, stator gradient, hot-spot and sensor uncertainty).

derived_requirements.label: Gross permanent-magnet temperature headroom above coolant inlet
derived_requirements.basis: 150 °C magnet limit − 60 °C stated coolant inlet = 90 K gross headroom including all rotor-to-coolant gradients.

derived_requirements.label: First-pass combined cassette peak heat-rejection duty
derived_requirements.basis: Transparent first-pass: 95% overall efficiency at 350 kW hardware throughput → loss = 350 × (1/0.95 − 1) ≈ 18.4 kW. Corresponding 250 kW regen export loss is lower (~13 kW class). Not a continuous rating without a duty time history. Companion expansions used ~20 kW (regen-loss breakdown) and ~25 kW (~93% combined); values were not averaged.

derived_requirements.label: Rotor-to-differential reduction ratio
derived_requirements.basis: Brief requires single-speed reduction inside the hollow rotor but does not give tyre rolling radius, vehicle top speed, or permitted front-wheel overspeed. Independent expansions invented 7.6:1 and 7.8:1 from unstated tyre/speed assumptions; those numeric claims are dropped pending chassis/tyre data.

derived_requirements.label: Peak total axle torque (both halfshafts)
derived_requirements.basis: Cannot be fixed until reduction ratio, low-speed motor torque envelope, gear efficiency, and traction-control limits are specified. Expansions that reported ~2450–2500 Nm depended on assumed base speed (~10,000 rpm) and assumed gear ratio — not brief facts.

derived_requirements.label: Maximum continuous duration of an enabled front-traction window
derived_requirements.basis: Brief identifies starts, Attack Mode and qualifying windows but gives neither duration, front kW split, nor repetitions. Required for thermal inventory and continuous-current sizing.

parsedBrief.original_text:
# Formula E Gen3 / Gen3 Evo Front Powertrain Kit (FPK) — Demo Brief

**Product class (Anvil):** `formula_e_front_mgu` — the deliverable is the **spec front MGU + inverter + single-speed reduction + differential** as one unit (Front Powertrain Kit / FPK). This is **not** the rear manufacturer MGU, not a full race car, and not a road-car EDU paste.

**Demo role:** This class is the **JLR / Formula E demo artefact** to zip. The rear class (`formula_e_rear_mgu`) remains a process artefact.

---

## Form follows the front-axle bay (load-bearing)

The shape of this system is **not free**. It is forced by the **available packaging volume where the FPK must live on the front axle** of the Spark Gen3 / Gen3 Evo car:

- Wishbone / upright / steering clearance
- Crash structure and nose box behind
- Halfshaft exit height and track
- Cooling / HV / LV routing corridors to the front of the car
- Ground clearance and aero floor above

**Morphology rule:** size and silhouette are set by that **front-axle bay envelope** first; internal motor / inverter / gear volumes then pack into that bay. Lucid/Atieva gold imagery is a **TRAINING CHECK** that a bay-constrained unitised pack looks like real race hardware — never a mesh paste of proprietary CAD.

Public press envelope (Lucid IR / media; inch→mm checked):

| Axis | Press (in) | mm | Role in bay |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | 10.2 | **259** | Compact axis in bay |
| B | 13.5 | **343** | Lateral / track-related span |
| C | 10.5 | **267** | Vertical / package height (press often rounded 266) |

Treat `max_dimensions_mm` as the **homologated front bay box the unit must fit**. Do not invent a larger free-form silhouette.

---

## System description

- One front MGU (primarily generating on Gen3; Gen3 Evo adds limited AWD traction windows), liquid-cooled PMSM class
- Integrated SiC inverter / MCU in the same unitised housing
- Single-speed reduction + differential; halfshaft exits toward the front wheels
- Spec / common kit for all teams (Lucid / Atieva supplier lineage) — not manufacturer-free like the rear
- Cooling, HV DC, and control interfaces face the corridors available in the front bay

---

## Key constraints (public Gen3 / Gen3 Evo + press)

Fact-checked 2026-07-29 via OpenRouter (Kimi K3 + GLM 5.2 + SOL) against public FIA / Formula E / Lucid press. Caveats retained.

| Constraint | Value | Provenance / note |
|---|---|---|
| Supplier | Lucid / Atieva FPK | CONFIRM — Gen3 front powertrain tender / Lucid IR |
| Unit dry mass (press) | **~32 kg** | CONFIRM press; boundary of fluids/harness unclear |
| Bay envelope | **259 × 343 × 267 mm** | CONFIRM inch conversion; press-derived |
| Peak motor speed (press) | **~19,500 rpm** | Press-repeat; FIA allows up to ~20,000 rpm class |
| Front regen (Gen3) | **≤ 250 kW** electrical | CONFIRM — pairs with ≤350 kW rear → ≤600 kW total regen |
| Hardware power class (press) | **~350 kW** cited | Press / density PR (14.7 hp/kg @ 32 kg); clarify electrical vs mechanical in tools |
| Gen3 front role | Regen / energy recovery | CONFIRM — no traction |
| Gen3 Evo front role | Regen + limited AWD traction windows | CONFIRM — starts / Attack Mode / qualifying duels (split kW not always public) |
| Public STEP/CAD | **None** | CONFIRM — gold = sealed-unit press photography |
| Road-car Lucid Tech Talk / patents | Physics training only | CONFIRM — cooling/winding principles, not FE mesh |

### Brief metrics (exact keys for compliance)

| key_metric | value | unit |
|---|---:|---|
| `front_regen_electrical_cap_kw` | 250 | kW |
| `front_hardware_power_class_kw` | 350 | kW |
| `max_rotor_speed_rpm` | 19500 | rpm |
| `fpk_mass_cap_kg` | 32 | kg |
| `front_bay_envelope_w_mm` | 343 | mm |
| `front_bay_envelope_d_mm` | 259 | mm |
| `front_bay_envelope_h_mm` | 267 | mm |
| `assumed_vdc_min_v` | 600 | V |
| `assumed_vdc_max_v` | 900 | V |
| `assumed_coolant_inlet_c` | 60 | °C |
| `winding_temp_limit_c` | 180 | °C |
| `magnet_temp_limit_c` | 150 | °C |

### Envelope (hard packaging)

```
max_dimensions_mm:
  width:  343   # lateral — halfshaft / track axis class
  depth:  259   # fore-aft in bay
  height: 267   # vertical package
max_mass_kg: 32
```

Orientation note for twin: treat **width as car-lateral** (shaft exits ±X) so exterior cameras see barrel + unitised brick faces, consistent with bay packing.

---

## Morphology / FFF (universal, bay-first)

1. **Bay box wins** — every exterior volume must fit inside `max_dimensions_mm`; no apron larger than the bay.
2. **Concentric integrated stack** (public FE FPK packaging grammar — Lucid/Atieva press = TRAINING CHECK, never CAD paste):
   - **L1 MCU/SiC** — bolts to flat upper shelf; solid phase busbars pierce into stator (no long HV AC cables).
   - **L2 Stator** — outer cylindrical ring; wave-wound copper class; end-winding microjet oil cooling for extreme regen.
   - **L3 Hollow rotor** — PM barrel nested in stator ID; bore hosts the transmission.
   - **L4 Planetary + mini-diff** — inside the rotor cavity; torque out to ±X axle sockets.
3. **Unitised sealed exterior** — one cassette silhouette; reduction/diff are *inside* the rotor, not a separate side box.
4. **Shaft ends** — halfshaft exits define lateral width and case splits.
5. **Service faces** — coolant bosses + HV/LV on faces that reach front-bay corridors.
6. **Gold check** — Lucid sealed-unit press photos / anatomy write-ups: if function + bay + concentric stack are right, morphology should look *very similar*; never STEP/mesh paste.
7. **PCB / windings / planetary guts** — cutaway / ghost only on sealed exterior views.

---

## Out of scope

- Rear manufacturer MGU/MCU (see `formula_e_rear_mgu`)
- Full car, battery, chassis crash structure detail
- Copying Lucid proprietary CAD or road Air EDU silhouette as a paste target
- Separate "sources → search → formulas" demo report — result is better images in the design-pack zip

brief_expansion.notes:
Product identity: homologated motorsport front powertrain cassette (spec kit for all teams), not a road-car EDU and not the rear manufacturer MGU. Mass cap 32 kg and bay box 343×259×267 mm are stated commercial/homologation limits.

Conflicts resolved:
- Peak heat rejection: expansions gave ~18.4 kW (95% @ 350 kW), ~20 kW (regen loss breakdown @ 250 kW), and ~25 kW (~93% @ 350 kW). Did not average; kept 18.4 kW as transparent first-pass with confidence low.
- Peak AC phase current: ~520 A_rms vs ~550 A_rms from different pf/η assumptions; kept 520 with medium confidence and recorded the alternate.
- Gear ratio: 7.8 vs 7.6 vs explicit null. Brief lacks tyre radius and top speed; numeric ratios dropped (value null).
- Peak axle/wheel torque: ~2450 Nm vs ~2500 Nm vs null — both numerics depended on assumed base speed and ratio; set null.
- Coolant flow: 40 L/min (water-glycol), 44 L/min (dielectric oil), and 1.74 m³/h external water-glycol — incompatible fluid/ΔT assumptions; all specific flow numbers dropped.
- Hardware power class treated as stated 350 kW sizing duty; electrical vs mechanical label remains to be fixed in the interface spec (flagged in basis).

Dropped (single-expansion claims without brief support): rotor tip speed; rotor overspeed proof rpm; bearing DN; end-winding microjet oil flow; max fundamental frequency / pole-count assumption; inverter switching frequency; continuous/lap-RMS heat rejection; regen energy per braking event; sealed-cassette service life km; peak rotor torque at assumed 10,000 rpm base speed; regen shaft torque at max speed with assumed efficiency; external coolant flow numerics; mount reaction torque null already covered by axle-torque null; packaging volume in m³ duplicate of 23.7 L.

No proprietary Lucid CAD. Press envelope is a training/packaging check only. Gen3 Evo front traction kW split and window durations remain non-public and block final thermal and fatigue closure.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The power distribution module routes high-voltage electrical energy from the DC source to the traction inverters and motor-generator units. DC power at a nominal 750 V bus voltage, bounded between 600 V and 900 V, enters through the Hv DC Fuse assembly that includes the Hv DC Busbar Link and Connector Interlock Pin to provide over-current protection and safe isolation. Three-phase AC output is then carried by the AC Phase Busbar Pierce together with its Shield Drain Bond, sized for a maximum phase current of 477 A and continuous power of 250 kW. The arrangement supports a front hardware power class of 350 kW and rear axle electrical power of 350 kW while limiting total dissipation to 6.63 kW under continuous duty, with coolant flow maintained at 12 L/min to keep component temperatures within limits. The module thereby delivers protected, high-integrity power transfer across the vehicle drivetrain.

sub_modules.name_human: Power Distribution — Hv DC Fuse group
sub_modules.english_sentence: The HV DC fuse, laminated HV DC busbar link and connector interlock pins form the cassette’s DC entry path. A Mersen/Littelfuse-class 900 V EV fuse protects the 250 kW regen export (416.7 A at 600 V, 277.8 A at 900 V) and the 583 A peak hardware bus current, while the copper laminated busbar keeps inductance low into the DC-link film bank on the SiC shelf. Gold-plated HVIL interlock pins in the connector open the safety loop before power contacts separate, satisfying ISO 6469-3 and FIA FE electrical rules inside the front-bay HV corridor without adding depth beyond 259 mm.

sub_modules.name_human: Power Distribution — AC Phase Busbar Pierce group
sub_modules.english_sentence: The AC phase busbar pierce set is three solid copper phase conductors that leave the SiC inverter shelf and enter the stator terminals directly, eliminating long HV AC cables in the bay. Each bar is insulated for 535–550 A_rms phase current at up to 650 Hz fundamental and sealed where it passes the housing web. Shield drain bonds tie the HV shield cover and cable shields to chassis earth so EMC currents return cleanly despite the dense front-bay routing of coolant, LV and HV services.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The energy conversion transduction module accepts 750 V DC bus power and delivers up to 350 kW continuous output to the motor-generator unit. Within the silicon carbide (SiC) traction inverter, the SiC power module stack switches the DC link capacitor bank through the gate driver board housed in the inverter housing and cover, achieving 0.988 efficiency while dissipating 6.63 kW under continuous load. Coolant enters at 60 °C and flows at 12 L/min through the ports, limiting winding temperature to 86.8 °C. The phase current sensor, fitted with high-voltage DC and low-voltage signal connectors, measures output currents reaching 477 A and feeds real-time data to the controller for torque regulation. The module thereby converts and conditions electrical power for traction while maintaining thermal and electrical limits within the 343 mm × 259 mm × 267 mm envelope.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The control compute communication module coordinates inverter operation through the OEM Inverter Control Board fitted with a CAN FD vehicle interface, an HV interlock interface, a resolver signal interface and a control harness set. The board receives torque and speed demands over the vehicle bus, validates safety interlocks and resolver position data, then issues gate commands while the DC bus voltage is held at 750 V and phase current is limited to 477 A. Continuous electrical power of 250 kW is sustained with traction inverter power reaching 350 kW and inverter efficiency of 0.988, delivering MGU shaft power of 244 kW at base speeds up to 19 500 rpm. Coolant flow of 12 L/min maintains winding temperature at 86.8 °C, well below the 180 °C limit. The OEM Inverter Control Board therefore supplies the sole interface between vehicle commands and the power stage, enforcing all protection and modulation functions.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The sensing instrumentation acquires precise measurements of electrical and thermal conditions across the drive unit. The voltage sensor integrates a current sensor, temperature probe, pressure sensor and signal conditioner to capture dc bus voltage at 750 V, phase currents up to 477 A and coolant outlet temperature of 69.1 °C during continuous operation at 250 kW. These elements also monitor flow at 12 L/min and track winding and magnet temperatures against limits of 180 °C and 150 °C respectively, while the signal conditioner prepares data for the control system. All readings remain within the design envelope of 343 mm width, 259 mm depth and 267 mm height. The module supplies the verified measurements required for safe and efficient traction performance.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The actuation kinematics module converts dc electrical power into mechanical shaft torque for traction. Incoming power at 750 V and up to 250 kW continuous is fed to the Traction Ipmsm Motor Generator, which houses the stator laminations, windings, outer casing, cooling jacket and reduction gear stage arranged at an 8:1 ratio. This assembly accepts 247 kW ac electrical input and produces 244 kW at the shaft while limiting total dissipation to 6.63 kW under a 12 L/min coolant flow that raises temperature by 9.1 K. The Permanent Magnet Set, comprising the hollow rotor barrel, motor shaft, front and rear bearings and end bells, rotates at 19500 rpm within a 123 mm airgap to deliver 120 Nm continuous torque at 0.99 efficiency. The integrated unit weighs 28.8 kg and occupies a 343 mm × 259 mm × 267 mm envelope. The module thereby supplies 237 kW gear output for vehicle propulsion under the specified thermal and speed limits.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The structure containment module centres on the Traction Drive Housing that encloses the motor-generator unit, inverter and reduction gear. Fabricated to a total mass of 28.8 kg and an internal volume of 0.0237 m³, the housing maintains the assembly within a front-bay envelope 343 mm wide, 259 mm deep and 267 mm high while withstanding continuous electrical input of 250 kW and peak shaft power of 244 kW at 19500 rpm. Coolant circulated at 12 L/min limits winding temperature to 86.8 °C and magnet temperature to 102 °C under a 9.1 K rise, dissipating 6.63 kW of continuous losses. High-voltage shielding, cassette covers and mounting ears secure the 750 V dc bus and 477 A phase-current paths against vibration and electromagnetic interference. The single sub-module therefore supplies the mechanical envelope, thermal management interfaces and safety barriers required by the integrated traction drive.

sub_modules.english_sentence: The traction drive housing is a cast and machined aluminium sealed cassette that defines the entire FPK silhouette inside the 343×259×267 mm homologated front bay (0.023719 m³). It carries the cassette cover, HV shield cover, mounting ear set and fastener set so the concentric L1 SiC shelf, L2 stator, L3 hollow rotor and L4 planetary-plus-mini-diff stack bolt into one structural oil-and-glycol-tight unit at 28.8 kg tool mass versus the 32 kg cap. Mounting ears react halfshaft and regen torque into the Spark subframe without aprons beyond the bay keep-outs, while the HV shield cover breaks the HVIL loop when removed. Nameplate marking identifies the Lucid/Atieva-lineage common kit for all Formula E teams. IP6K9K exterior sealing protects dielectric oil and electronics from track water and debris. It comprises Traction Motor, Traction Inverter.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The safety protection module monitors and safeguards the high-voltage traction chain against electrical and thermal faults. The Hv Interlock Loop forms the central protective arrangement, combining phase overcurrent trip, inverter desat protection, coolant flow interlock and isolation monitor interface to detect anomalies in current, voltage, coolant circulation and insulation resistance. It continuously supervises the traction inverter and motor generator unit that operate at a dc bus voltage of 750 V with phase currents reaching 477 A, while also confirming adequate coolant flow of 12 L/min and winding temperatures remaining below 180 °C. Any breach of these limits opens the interlock, isolating the system before component stress can develop. The Hv Interlock Loop therefore supplies the primary safety function for the complete powertrain assembly.

modules.overview_paragraph_en: The environmental interface regulates temperatures within the motor generator unit and motor control unit during continuous 250 kW operation. Waste heat of 6.63 kW is extracted by coolant that enters at 60 °C, rises by 9.1 K and leaves at 69.1 °C while flowing at 12 L/min. The Mgu Cold Plate integrates the Mgu Cold Plate, Mcu Cold Plate, Coolant Manifold, Coolant Hose Set and Coolant Expansion Bottle into a single primary cooling circuit sized for the front powertrain bay. Channel velocities reach 15.9 m/s with a 71.1 kPa pressure drop, keeping winding and magnet temperatures at 86.8 °C and 102 °C respectively. These values remain comfortably below the 180 °C and 150 °C limits while the unit mass stays at 28.8 kg inside the 343 mm × 259 mm × 267 mm envelope. The module thereby sustains continuous power delivery without thermal excursion.

power_distribution.paragraph_en: The Power Distribution module organises 2 sub-modules (Power Distribution — Hv DC Fuse group, Power Distribution — AC Phase Busbar Pierce group) with 1 internal DC to AC power path link. The HV DC fuse, laminated HV DC busbar link and connector interlock pins form the cassette’s DC entry path. A Mersen/Littelfuse-class 900 V EV fuse protects the 250 kW regen export (416.7 A at 600 V, 277.8 A at 900 V) and the 583 A peak hardware bus current, while the copper laminated busbar keeps inductance low into the DC-link film bank on the SiC shelf. Gold-plated HVIL interlock pins in the connector open the safety loop before power contacts separate, satisfying ISO 6469-3 and FIA FE electrical rules inside the front-bay HV corridor without adding depth beyond 259 mm. The AC phase busbar pierce set is three solid copper phase conductors that leave the SiC inverter shelf and enter the stator terminals directly, eliminating long HV AC cables in the bay. Each bar is insulated for 535–550 A_rms phase current at up to 650 Hz fundamental and sealed where it passes the housing web. Shield drain bonds tie the HV shield cover and cable shields to chassis earth so EMC currents return cleanly despite the dense front-bay routing of coolant, LV and HV services. The Power Distribution — Hv DC Fuse group drives the Power Distribution — AC Phase Busbar Pierce group via DC to AC power path (HV DC fuse and busbar feed inverter; AC pierce bars leave inverter into stator.).

power_distribution.paragraph_en_llm: The power distribution module routes high-voltage electrical energy from the DC source to the traction inverters and motor-generator units. DC power at a nominal 750 V bus voltage, bounded between 600 V and 900 V, enters through the Hv DC Fuse assembly that includes the Hv DC Busbar Link and Connector Interlock Pin to provide over-current protection and safe isolation. Three-phase AC output is then carried by the AC Phase Busbar Pierce together with its Shield Drain Bond, sized for a maximum phase current of 477 A and continuous power of 250 kW. The arrangement supports a front hardware power class of 350 kW and rear axle electrical power of 350 kW while limiting total dissipation to 6.63 kW under continuous duty, with coolant flow maintained at 12 L/min to keep component temperatures within limits. The module thereby delivers protected, high-integrity power transfer across the vehicle drivetrain.

energy_conversion_transduction.paragraph_en_llm: The energy conversion transduction module accepts 750 V DC bus power and delivers up to 350 kW continuous output to the motor-generator unit. Within the silicon carbide (SiC) traction inverter, the SiC power module stack switches the DC link capacitor bank through the gate driver board housed in the inverter housing and cover, achieving 0.988 efficiency while dissipating 6.63 kW under continuous load. Coolant enters at 60 °C and flows at 12 L/min through the ports, limiting winding temperature to 86.8 °C. The phase current sensor, fitted with high-voltage DC and low-voltage signal connectors, measures output currents reaching 477 A and feeds real-time data to the controller for torque regulation. The module thereby converts and conditions electrical power for traction while maintaining thermal and electrical limits within the 343 mm × 259 mm × 267 mm envelope.

control_compute_communication.paragraph_en_llm: The control compute communication module coordinates inverter operation through the OEM Inverter Control Board fitted with a CAN FD vehicle interface, an HV interlock interface, a resolver signal interface and a control harness set. The board receives torque and speed demands over the vehicle bus, validates safety interlocks and resolver position data, then issues gate commands while the DC bus voltage is held at 750 V and phase current is limited to 477 A. Continuous electrical power of 250 kW is sustained with traction inverter power reaching 350 kW and inverter efficiency of 0.988, delivering MGU shaft power of 244 kW at base speeds up to 19 500 rpm. Coolant flow of 12 L/min maintains winding temperature at 86.8 °C, well below the 180 °C limit. The OEM Inverter Control Board therefore supplies the sole interface between vehicle commands and the power stage, enforcing all protection and modulation functions.

sensing_instrumentation.paragraph_en_llm: The sensing instrumentation acquires precise measurements of electrical and thermal conditions across the drive unit. The voltage sensor integrates a current sensor, temperature probe, pressure sensor and signal conditioner to capture dc bus voltage at 750 V, phase currents up to 477 A and coolant outlet temperature of 69.1 °C during continuous operation at 250 kW. These elements also monitor flow at 12 L/min and track winding and magnet temperatures against limits of 180 °C and 150 °C respectively, while the signal conditioner prepares data for the control system. All readings remain within the design envelope of 343 mm width, 259 mm depth and 267 mm height. The module supplies the verified measurements required for safe and efficient traction performance.

actuation_kinematics.paragraph_en_llm: The actuation kinematics module converts dc electrical power into mechanical shaft torque for traction. Incoming power at 750 V and up to 250 kW continuous is fed to the Traction Ipmsm Motor Generator, which houses the stator laminations, windings, outer casing, cooling jacket and reduction gear stage arranged at an 8:1 ratio. This assembly accepts 247 kW ac electrical input and produces 244 kW at the shaft while limiting total dissipation to 6.63 kW under a 12 L/min coolant flow that raises temperature by 9.1 K. The Permanent Magnet Set, comprising the hollow rotor barrel, motor shaft, front and rear bearings and end bells, rotates at 19500 rpm within a 123 mm airgap to deliver 120 Nm continuous torque at 0.99 efficiency. The integrated unit weighs 28.8 kg and occupies a 343 mm × 259 mm × 267 mm envelope. The module thereby supplies 237 kW gear output for vehicle propulsion under the specified thermal and speed limits.

structure_containment.paragraph_en: The Structure / Containment module organises Structure Containment. The traction drive housing is a cast and machined aluminium sealed cassette that defines the entire FPK silhouette inside the 343×259×267 mm homologated front bay (0.023719 m³). It carries the cassette cover, HV shield cover, mounting ear set and fastener set so the concentric L1 SiC shelf, L2 stator, L3 hollow rotor and L4 planetary-plus-mini-diff stack bolt into one structural oil-and-glycol-tight unit at 28.8 kg tool mass versus the 32 kg cap. Mounting ears react halfshaft and regen torque into the Spark subframe without aprons beyond the bay keep-outs, while the HV shield cover breaks the HVIL loop when removed. Nameplate marking identifies the Lucid/Atieva-lineage common kit for all Formula E teams. IP6K9K exterior sealing protects dielectric oil and electronics from track water and debris.

structure_containment.paragraph_en_llm: The structure containment module centres on the Traction Drive Housing that encloses the motor-generator unit, inverter and reduction gear. Fabricated to a total mass of 28.8 kg and an internal volume of 0.0237 m³, the housing maintains the assembly within a front-bay envelope 343 mm wide, 259 mm deep and 267 mm high while withstanding continuous electrical input of 250 kW and peak shaft power of 244 kW at 19500 rpm. Coolant circulated at 12 L/min limits winding temperature to 86.8 °C and magnet temperature to 102 °C under a 9.1 K rise, dissipating 6.63 kW of continuous losses. High-voltage shielding, cassette covers and mounting ears secure the 750 V dc bus and 477 A phase-current paths against vibration and electromagnetic interference. The single sub-module therefore supplies the mechanical envelope, thermal management interfaces and safety barriers required by the integrated traction drive.

safety_protection.paragraph_en_llm: The safety protection module monitors and safeguards the high-voltage traction chain against electrical and thermal faults. The Hv Interlock Loop forms the central protective arrangement, combining phase overcurrent trip, inverter desat protection, coolant flow interlock and isolation monitor interface to detect anomalies in current, voltage, coolant circulation and insulation resistance. It continuously supervises the traction inverter and motor generator unit that operate at a dc bus voltage of 750 V with phase currents reaching 477 A, while also confirming adequate coolant flow of 12 L/min and winding temperatures remaining below 180 °C. Any breach of these limits opens the interlock, isolating the system before component stress can develop. The Hv Interlock Loop therefore supplies the primary safety function for the complete powertrain assembly.

environmental_interface.paragraph_en_llm: The environmental interface regulates temperatures within the motor generator unit and motor control unit during continuous 250 kW operation. Waste heat of 6.63 kW is extracted by coolant that enters at 60 °C, rises by 9.1 K and leaves at 69.1 °C while flowing at 12 L/min. The Mgu Cold Plate integrates the Mgu Cold Plate, Mcu Cold Plate, Coolant Manifold, Coolant Hose Set and Coolant Expansion Bottle into a single primary cooling circuit sized for the front powertrain bay. Channel velocities reach 15.9 m/s with a 71.1 kPa pressure drop, keeping winding and magnet temperatures at 86.8 °C and 102 °C respectively. These values remain comfortably below the 180 °C and 150 °C limits while the unit mass stays at 28.8 kg inside the 343 mm × 259 mm × 267 mm envelope. The module thereby sustains continuous power delivery without thermal excursion.

orchestratorContract.brief_summary: Formula E Gen3/Evo SPEC front FPK (unitised MGU+inverter+gear+diff) — bay envelope 343×259×267 mm forces form; ~32 kg; ≤250 kW front regen (HW class ~350 kW press). Rear manufacturer MGU out of scope.

front_hardware_power_class_kw.source_detail: FRONT unit SURVIVABILITY ENVELOPE — HW nameplate class (press): machine, inverter and gears must survive this even where software-limited. NOT continuous duty; the duty is front_regen_electrical_cap_kw = 250 kW. Sets phase_current_max_a = 477 A, which every FE torque solve, demag screen and copper-loss figure in this campaign ran at — do not collapse it to the duty without re-deriving all of them.

rear_axle_electrical_power_kw.source_detail: ALIAS of front_hardware_power_class_kw for the shared IPMSM/SiC tool pack (PEAK sizing). NOT an independent rear-axle measurement and NOT evidence about the rear motor — it is the FRONT unit's survivability envelope under a rear-sounding key. Over-predicting: the Steinmetz form is fitted below saturation and the yoke sits at 2.10 T, outside that fit (-25 to -40% on hysteresis). The true figure may sit roughly 0.65x to 1.4x this value. What is MEASURED is the FLUX; the LOSS is modelled from it. brief.original_text:
# Formula E Gen3 / Gen3 Evo Front Powertrain Kit (FPK) — Demo Brief

**Product class (Anvil):** `formula_e_front_mgu` — the deliverable is the **spec front MGU + inverter + single-speed reduction + differential** as one unit (Front Powertrain Kit / FPK). This is **not** the rear manufacturer MGU, not a full race car, and not a road-car EDU paste.

**Demo role:** This class is the **JLR / Formula E demo artefact** to zip. The rear class (`formula_e_rear_mgu`) remains a process artefact.

---

## Form follows the front-axle bay (load-bearing)

The shape of this system is **not free**. It is forced by the **available packaging volume where the FPK must live on the front axle** of the Spark Gen3 / Gen3 Evo car:

- Wishbone / upright / steering clearance
- Crash structure and nose box behind
- Halfshaft exit height and track
- Cooling / HV / LV routing corridors to the front of the car
- Ground clearance and aero floor above

**Morphology rule:** size and silhouette are set by that **front-axle bay envelope** first; internal motor / inverter / gear volumes then pack into that bay. Lucid/Atieva gold imagery is a **TRAINING CHECK** that a bay-constrained unitised pack looks like real race hardware — never a mesh paste of proprietary CAD.

Public press envelope (Lucid IR / media; inch→mm checked):

| Axis | Press (in) | mm | Role in bay |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | 10.2 | **259** | Compact axis in bay |
| B | 13.5 | **343** | Lateral / track-related span |
| C | 10.5 | **267** | Vertical / package height (press often rounded 266) |

Treat `max_dimensions_mm` as the **homologated front bay box the unit must fit**. Do not invent a larger free-form silhouette.

---

## System description

- One front MGU (primarily generating on Gen3; Gen3 Evo adds limited AWD traction windows), liquid-cooled PMSM class
- Integrated SiC inverter / MCU in the same unitised housing
- Single-speed reduction + differential; halfshaft exits toward the front wheels
- Spec / common kit for all teams (Lucid / Atieva supplier lineage) — not manufacturer-free like the rear
- Cooling, HV DC, and control interfaces face the corridors available in the front bay

---

## Key constraints (public Gen3 / Gen3 Evo + press)

Fact-checked 2026-07-29 via OpenRouter (Kimi K3 + GLM 5.2 + SOL) against public FIA / Formula E / Lucid press. Caveats retained.

| Constraint | Value | Provenance / note |
|---|---|---|
| Supplier | Lucid / Atieva FPK | CONFIRM — Gen3 front powertrain tender / Lucid IR |
| Unit dry mass (press) | **~32 kg** | CONFIRM press; boundary of fluids/harness unclear |
| Bay envelope | **259 × 343 × 267 mm** | CONFIRM inch conversion; press-derived |
| Peak motor speed (press) | **~19,500 rpm** | Press-repeat; FIA allows up to ~20,000 rpm class |
| Front regen (Gen3) | **≤ 250 kW** electrical | CONFIRM — pairs with ≤350 kW rear → ≤600 kW total regen |
| Hardware power class (press) | **~350 kW** cited | Press / density PR (14.7 hp/kg @ 32 kg); clarify electrical vs mechanical in tools |
| Gen3 front role | Regen / energy recovery | CONFIRM — no traction |
| Gen3 Evo front role | Regen + limited AWD traction windows | CONFIRM — starts / Attack Mode / qualifying duels (split kW not always public) |
| Public STEP/CAD | **None** | CONFIRM — gold = sealed-unit press photography |
| Road-car Lucid Tech Talk / patents | Physics training only | CONFIRM — cooling/winding principles, not FE mesh |

### Brief metrics (exact keys for compliance)

| key_metric | value | unit |
|---|---:|---|
| `front_regen_electrical_cap_kw` | 250 | kW |
| `front_hardware_power_class_kw` | 350 | kW |
| `max_rotor_speed_rpm` | 19500 | rpm |
| `fpk_mass_cap_kg` | 32 | kg |
| `front_bay_envelope_w_mm` | 343 | mm |
| `front_bay_envelope_d_mm` | 259 | mm |
| `front_bay_envelope_h_mm` | 267 | mm |
| `assumed_vdc_min_v` | 600 | V |
| `assumed_vdc_max_v` | 900 | V |
| `assumed_coolant_inlet_c` | 60 | °C |
| `winding_temp_limit_c` | 180 | °C |
| `magnet_temp_limit_c` | 150 | °C |

### Envelope (hard packaging)

```
max_dimensions_mm:
  width:  343   # lateral — halfshaft / track axis class
  depth:  259   # fore-aft in bay
  height: 267   # vertical package
max_mass_kg: 32
```

Orientation note for twin: treat **width as car-lateral** (shaft exits ±X) so exterior cameras see barrel + unitised brick faces, consistent with bay packing.

---

## Morphology / FFF (universal, bay-first)

1. **Bay box wins** — every exterior volume must fit inside `max_dimensions_mm`; no apron larger than the bay.
2. **Concentric integrated stack** (public FE FPK packaging grammar — Lucid/Atieva press = TRAINING CHECK, never CAD paste):
   - **L1 MCU/SiC** — bolts to flat upper shelf; solid phase busbars pierce into stator (no long HV AC cables).
   - **L2 Stator** — outer cylindrical ring; wave-wound copper class; end-winding microjet oil cooling for extreme regen.
   - **L3 Hollow rotor** — PM barrel nested in stator ID; bore hosts the transmission.
   - **L4 Planetary + mini-diff** — inside the rotor cavity; torque out to ±X axle sockets.
3. **Unitised sealed exterior** — one cassette silhouette; reduction/diff are *inside* the rotor, not a separate side box.
4. **Shaft ends** — halfshaft exits define lateral width and case splits.
5. **Service faces** — coolant bosses + HV/LV on faces that reach front-bay corridors.
6. **Gold check** — Lucid sealed-unit press photos / anatomy write-ups: if function + bay + concentric stack are right, morphology should look *very similar*; never STEP/mesh paste.
7. **PCB / windings / planetary guts** — cutaway / ghost only on sealed exterior views.

---

## Out of scope

- Rear manufacturer MGU/MCU (see `formula_e_rear_mgu`)
- Full car, battery, chassis crash structure detail
- Copying Lucid proprietary CAD or road Air EDU silhouette as a paste target
- Separate "sources → search → formulas" demo report — result is better images in the design-pack zip

Cooling, HV DC, and control interfaces must face corridors available in the front bay; no exterior apron larger than bay box.

parsed_original.original_text:
# Formula E Gen3 / Gen3 Evo Front Powertrain Kit (FPK) — Demo Brief

**Product class (Anvil):** `formula_e_front_mgu` — the deliverable is the **spec front MGU + inverter + single-speed reduction + differential** as one unit (Front Powertrain Kit / FPK). This is **not** the rear manufacturer MGU, not a full race car, and not a road-car EDU paste.

**Demo role:** This class is the **JLR / Formula E demo artefact** to zip. The rear class (`formula_e_rear_mgu`) remains a process artefact.

---

## Form follows the front-axle bay (load-bearing)

The shape of this system is **not free**. It is forced by the **available packaging volume where the FPK must live on the front axle** of the Spark Gen3 / Gen3 Evo car:

- Wishbone / upright / steering clearance
- Crash structure and nose box behind
- Halfshaft exit height and track
- Cooling / HV / LV routing corridors to the front of the car
- Ground clearance and aero floor above

**Morphology rule:** size and silhouette are set by that **front-axle bay envelope** first; internal motor / inverter / gear volumes then pack into that bay. Lucid/Atieva gold imagery is a **TRAINING CHECK** that a bay-constrained unitised pack looks like real race hardware — never a mesh paste of proprietary CAD.

Public press envelope (Lucid IR / media; inch→mm checked):

| Axis | Press (in) | mm | Role in bay |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | 10.2 | **259** | Compact axis in bay |
| B | 13.5 | **343** | Lateral / track-related span |
| C | 10.5 | **267** | Vertical / package height (press often rounded 266) |

Treat `max_dimensions_mm` as the **homologated front bay box the unit must fit**. Do not invent a larger free-form silhouette.

---

## System description

- One front MGU (primarily generating on Gen3; Gen3 Evo adds limited AWD traction windows), liquid-cooled PMSM class
- Integrated SiC inverter / MCU in the same unitised housing
- Single-speed reduction + differential; halfshaft exits toward the front wheels
- Spec / common kit for all teams (Lucid / Atieva supplier lineage) — not manufacturer-free like the rear
- Cooling, HV DC, and control interfaces face the corridors available in the front bay

---

## Key constraints (public Gen3 / Gen3 Evo + press)

Fact-checked 2026-07-29 via OpenRouter (Kimi K3 + GLM 5.2 + SOL) against public FIA / Formula E / Lucid press. Caveats retained.

| Constraint | Value | Provenance / note |
|---|---|---|
| Supplier | Lucid / Atieva FPK | CONFIRM — Gen3 front powertrain tender / Lucid IR |
| Unit dry mass (press) | **~32 kg** | CONFIRM press; boundary of fluids/harness unclear |
| Bay envelope | **259 × 343 × 267 mm** | CONFIRM inch conversion; press-derived |
| Peak motor speed (press) | **~19,500 rpm** | Press-repeat; FIA allows up to ~20,000 rpm class |
| Front regen (Gen3) | **≤ 250 kW** electrical | CONFIRM — pairs with ≤350 kW rear → ≤600 kW total regen |
| Hardware power class (press) | **~350 kW** cited | Press / density PR (14.7 hp/kg @ 32 kg); clarify electrical vs mechanical in tools |
| Gen3 front role | Regen / energy recovery | CONFIRM — no traction |
| Gen3 Evo front role | Regen + limited AWD traction windows | CONFIRM — starts / Attack Mode / qualifying duels (split kW not always public) |
| Public STEP/CAD | **None** | CONFIRM — gold = sealed-unit press photography |
| Road-car Lucid Tech Talk / patents | Physics training only | CONFIRM — cooling/winding principles, not FE mesh |

### Brief metrics (exact keys for compliance)

| key_metric | value | unit |
|---|---:|---|
| `front_regen_electrical_cap_kw` | 250 | kW |
| `front_hardware_power_class_kw` | 350 | kW |
| `max_rotor_speed_rpm` | 19500 | rpm |
| `fpk_mass_cap_kg` | 32 | kg |
| `front_bay_envelope_w_mm` | 343 | mm |
| `front_bay_envelope_d_mm` | 259 | mm |
| `front_bay_envelope_h_mm` | 267 | mm |
| `assumed_vdc_min_v` | 600 | V |
| `assumed_vdc_max_v` | 900 | V |
| `assumed_coolant_inlet_c` | 60 | °C |
| `winding_temp_limit_c` | 180 | °C |
| `magnet_temp_limit_c` | 150 | °C |

### Envelope (hard packaging)

```
max_dimensions_mm:
  width:  343   # lateral — halfshaft / track axis class
  depth:  259   # fore-aft in bay
  height: 267   # vertical package
max_mass_kg: 32
```

Orientation note for twin: treat **width as car-lateral** (shaft exits ±X) so exterior cameras see barrel + unitised brick faces, consistent with bay packing.

---

## Morphology / FFF (universal, bay-first)

1. **Bay box wins** — every exterior volume must fit inside `max_dimensions_mm`; no apron larger than the bay.
2. **Concentric integrated stack** (public FE FPK packaging grammar — Lucid/Atieva press = TRAINING CHECK, never CAD paste):
   - **L1 MCU/SiC** — bolts to flat upper shelf; solid phase busbars pierce into stator (no long HV AC cables).
   - **L2 Stator** — outer cylindrical ring; wave-wound copper class; end-winding microjet oil cooling for extreme regen.
   - **L3 Hollow rotor** — PM barrel nested in stator ID; bore hosts the transmission.
   - **L4 Planetary + mini-diff** — inside the rotor cavity; torque out to ±X axle sockets.
3. **Unitised sealed exterior** — one cassette silhouette; reduction/diff are *inside* the rotor, not a separate side box.
4. **Shaft ends** — halfshaft exits define lateral width and case splits.
5. **Service faces** — coolant bosses + HV/LV on faces that reach front-bay corridors.
6. **Gold check** — Lucid sealed-unit press photos / anatomy write-ups: if function + bay + concentric stack are right, morphology should look *very similar*; never STEP/mesh paste.
7. **PCB / windings / planetary guts** — cutaway / ghost only on sealed exterior views.

---

## Out of scope

- Rear manufacturer MGU/MCU (see `formula_e_rear_mgu`)
- Full car, battery, chassis crash structure detail
- Copying Lucid proprietary CAD or road Air EDU silhouette as a paste target
- Separate "sources → search → formulas" demo report — result is better images in the design-pack zip

brief_expansion.notes:
Product identity: homologated motorsport front powertrain cassette (spec kit for all teams), not a road-car EDU and not the rear manufacturer MGU. Mass cap 32 kg and bay box 343×259×267 mm are stated commercial/homologation limits.

Conflicts resolved:
- Peak heat rejection: expansions gave ~18.4 kW (95% @ 350 kW), ~20 kW (regen loss breakdown @ 250 kW), and ~25 kW (~93% @ 350 kW). Did not average; kept 18.4 kW as transparent first-pass with confidence low.
- Peak AC phase current: ~520 A_rms vs ~550 A_rms from different pf/η assumptions; kept 520 with medium confidence and recorded the alternate.
- Gear ratio: 7.8 vs 7.6 vs explicit null. Brief lacks tyre radius and top speed; numeric ratios dropped (value null).
- Peak axle/wheel torque: ~2450 Nm vs ~2500 Nm vs null — both numerics depended on assumed base speed and ratio; set null.
- Coolant flow: 40 L/min (water-glycol), 44 L/min (dielectric oil), and 1.74 m³/h external water-glycol — incompatible fluid/ΔT assumptions; all specific flow numbers dropped.
- Hardware power class treated as stated 350 kW sizing duty; electrical vs mechanical label remains to be fixed in the interface spec (flagged in basis).

Dropped (single-expansion claims without brief support): rotor tip speed; rotor overspeed proof rpm; bearing DN; end-winding microjet oil flow; max fundamental frequency / pole-count assumption; inverter switching frequency; continuous/lap-RMS heat rejection; regen energy per braking event; sealed-cassette service life km; peak rotor torque at assumed 10,000 rpm base speed; regen shaft torque at max speed with assumed efficiency; external coolant flow numerics; mount reaction torque null already covered by axle-torque null; packaging volume in m³ duplicate of 23.7 L.

No proprietary Lucid CAD. Press envelope is a training/packaging check only. Gen3 Evo front traction kW split and window durations remain non-public and block final thermal and fatigue closure.

physicsCritique.headline: The design successfully packages the 350 kW front MGU within the tight Spark bay envelope, but contains several highly implausible industrial/data-center catalog parts.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'Hv DC Busbar Link' is assigned part number 'MKP1848C66012JY5' from Vishay Roederstein. This part number is actually a metallized polypropylene film capacitor (60 uF, 1200 V), not a physical copper busbar link.
issues.suggested_check: Replace with a custom copper busbar specification and move the Vishay part number exclusively to the DC Link Capacitor Bank.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'Phase Current Sensor' uses LEM part number 'HASS 100-S', which is a 100 A RMS (300 A peak) current sensor. The derived peak AC phase current for the 350 kW hardware class is 520 A_rms (up to 550 A_rms), meaning this sensor will saturate immediately under load.
issues.suggested_check: Replace with a sensor rated for at least 550 A_rms / 800 A peak, such as a motorsport-specific current transducer.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'Signal Conditioner' is specified as Weidmuller part '1481960000'. This is a bulky, industrial DIN-rail mounted signal converter (WAS5 PRO RTD) designed for electrical cabinets, which is completely unsuited for a highly integrated, space-constrained Formula E powertrain cassette.
issues.suggested_check: Replace with an integrated micro-electronics signal conditioning circuit designed directly onto the OEM Inverter Control Board.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'Coolant Manifold' is specified as 'Rack Manifold' from 'CoolIT Systems'. CoolIT Rack Manifolds are large, heavy stainless steel manifolds designed for liquid-cooled data center server racks, not a compact Formula E powertrain.
issues.suggested_check: Replace with a custom-machined or cast aluminium coolant manifold integrated directly into the MGU/MCU housing.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'Temperature Probe' is specified as Texas Instruments 'TMP1075DSGR', which is a digital silicon temperature sensor with a maximum operating limit of 125 °C. The design claims it operates up to 200 °C to monitor windings that have a 180 °C limit. The sensor will fail or melt at these temperatures.
issues.suggested_check: Replace with a PT100/PT1000 RTD or high-temperature NTC thermistor capable of surviving up to 200 °C.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'SiC Power Module Stack' is rated for 477 A, which is below the derived peak AC phase current requirement of 520 A_rms (and up to 550 A_rms) needed to deliver the 350 kW hardware power class at the minimum DC bus voltage of 600 V.
issues.suggested_check: Verify the peak current requirements and select a SiC module rated for at least 550 A_rms.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The 'Stator Windings' lists 'Siemens Gamesa' as the manufacturer. Siemens Gamesa is a manufacturer of utility-scale wind turbines, not high-performance motorsport stator windings.
issues.suggested_check: Change manufacturer to a motorsport-focused winding specialist or mark as custom/in-house.

issues.issue: ADVISORY (uncorroborated by deterministic check — visible, never scores): The inclusion of a 'Coolant Expansion Bottle' inside the sealed cassette is highly unusual. In Formula E, coolant expansion is handled by the vehicle's chassis-side cooling system, not inside the compact, sealed front powertrain cassette.
issues.suggested_check: Remove the expansion bottle from the cassette bill of materials and verify vehicle-side integration.

PRODUCT: Formula E Gen3/Gen3 Evo Front Powertrain Kit (FPK): a unitised front MGU with integrated SiC inverter, single-speed reduction and differential, packaged to the Spark front-axle bay. Spec common kit (Lucid/Atieva lineage) for regen on Gen3 and limited AWD traction windows on Gen3 Evo.

SUPPLIER ROLE: Subcontractor — compact reduction gear / final-drive stage.
WHAT THEY MUST DO: Supplies the compact reduction gear stage between MGU shaft and half-shaft / differential interface within the manufacturer perimeter.
KEY CAPABILITIES: high-speed reduction gear; motorsport final drive; compact planetary or parallel-axis gearset.
GEOGRAPHIC PREFERENCE: UK first, then EU. Open to East Asia for cell/PCBA-only roles.

power_distribution#0.intro: Two specialists are required to validate high-voltage electrical architecture and mechanical integration for the front motor generator unit power distribution module.

cards.background: Delivered high-voltage traction battery and inverter power distribution systems for high-performance electric racing vehicles, including busbar thermal management and safety interlock logic.
cards.typically_at: A high-performance electric vehicle powertrain consultancy
cards.covers: High-voltage busbars, fuses, and safety interlocks

questions.question: Does the High-voltage Direct Current Fuse rating account for peak transient currents during regenerative braking events?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Hv DC Fuse (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the fuse is sized for the specific peak current profile and thermal energy let-through of the inverter capacitor bank.

questions.question: Is the High-voltage Direct Current Busbar Link cross-section sufficient for continuous thermal duty at maximum motor torque?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Hv DC Busbar Link (basis.estimate_class = 4)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the cross-section is validated against steady-state current density limits to ensure temperature rise remains within insulation material ratings.

cards.background: Hands-on experience designing high-vibration electrical interconnects and shielding solutions for motorsport powertrains, specifically managing electromagnetic compatibility and structural integrity of busbar terminations.
cards.covers: Connector pins, busbar piercing, and shielding

questions.question: Does the Connector Interlock Pin geometry ensure reliable contact engagement under high-vibration conditions during race operation?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Connector Interlock Pin (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the pin geometry provides redundant contact points and sufficient spring force to maintain circuit continuity under specified vibration profiles.

questions.question: Is the Alternating Current Phase Busbar Pierce design optimised to prevent stress concentrations and fatigue failure at the…
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · AC Phase Busbar Pierce (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the pierce geometry includes stress-relief radii and is validated for fatigue life under the expected thermal expansion cycles.

energy_conversion_transduction#1.intro: Two specialists are required to validate the high-power electrical architecture and the thermal-mechanical enclosure design for the energy conversion module.

cards.specialist_role: A senior power electronics systems engineer
cards.background: Delivered high-voltage silicon carbide traction inverters for motorsport or aerospace applications, including gate driver integration and high-current busbar design.
cards.covers: Silicon carbide inverter, power stack, and gate driver board

questions.question: Does the silicon carbide power module stack thermal resistance meet our peak current switching requirements?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · SiC Power Module Stack (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the stack handles the specified current density while maintaining junction temperatures below the derating threshold for reliable operation.

questions.question: Is the gate driver board layout optimised to minimise parasitic inductance during high-frequency silicon carbide switching?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Gate Driver Board (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: The layout uses a Kelvin connection and minimised loop area to suppress voltage overshoot during rapid switching transitions.

cards.background: Designed liquid-cooled, high-vibration enclosures for automotive power electronics, specifically managing sealing, thermal interface materials, and high-voltage connector integration.
cards.typically_at: An electric vehicle powertrain equipment vendor
cards.covers: Inverter housing, cover, and coolant ports

questions.question: Does the inverter housing wall thickness provide sufficient structural rigidity to prevent vibration-induced fatigue failure?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Inverter Housing (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: Finite element analysis confirms the housing maintains structural integrity under the specified vibration profiles without exceeding material yield limits.

questions.question: Are the coolant port geometries optimised to ensure uniform flow distribution across the internal heat sink?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Coolant Port In (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: Computational fluid dynamics modelling confirms the port design eliminates stagnant zones and ensures consistent cooling across all power modules.

control_compute_communication#2.intro: Two specialists are required to validate the control architecture and safety-critical signal integrity for the front motor generator unit.

cards.background: Delivered high-speed motor control firmware and inverter gate-drive hardware for high-performance electric vehicle traction systems.
cards.covers: Inverter control and resolver signal processing

questions.question: Does the resolver signal interface specification provide sufficient noise immunity for high-speed motor position sensing?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Resolver Signal Interface (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, it specifies differential signalling and active filtering to maintain signal integrity against electromagnetic interference from the inverter.

questions.question: Is the original equipment manufacturer inverter control board architecture compatible with our required motor commutation latency?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Oem Inverter Control Board (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the board supports sub-microsecond interrupt response times necessary for stable field-oriented control at peak motor speeds.

cards.background: Designed Controller Area Network Flexible Data-rate communication architectures and high-voltage safety interlock systems for production electric vehicles.

questions.question: Does the Controller Area Network Flexible Data-rate interface meet the bandwidth requirements for real-time vehicle dynamics control?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Can Fd Vehicle Interface (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the interface supports five megabits per second, ensuring low-latency data exchange for the vehicle control unit.

questions.question: Are the high-voltage interlock interface and control harness set designed to meet international functional safety standards?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Hv Interlock Interface (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the design incorporates redundant loops and shielded cabling to ensure safe shutdown under all fault conditions.

sensing_instrumentation#3.intro: Two specialists are required to validate the sensing instrumentation design, focusing on electrical isolation and thermal measurement integrity for high-voltage motor systems.

cards.background: Delivered high-voltage isolation architectures for electric vehicle powertrains, specifically managing galvanic separation and signal integrity in high-electromagnetic-interference environments.

questions.question: Does the voltage sensor isolation rating exceed the maximum transient voltage of the motor controller?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Voltage Sensor (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, it provides reinforced isolation rated for double the peak bus voltage, ensuring safety during regenerative braking transients.

questions.question: Is the signal conditioner bandwidth sufficient to capture high-frequency switching noise without aliasing the primary signal?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Signal Conditioner (basis.estimate_class = 4)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the filter cutoff is optimised to reject switching noise while maintaining the required phase margin for control loops.

cards.background: Designed embedded sensor arrays for high-performance electric motors, focusing on thermal response times and mounting techniques for accurate stator temperature monitoring.

questions.question: Does the temperature probe response time meet the requirements for detecting rapid thermal spikes during peak power?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Temperature Probe (basis.estimate_class = 4)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the probe uses a low-mass tip design to ensure a time constant under two seconds for rapid transient detection.

questions.question: Is the probe mounting method robust against the vibration profiles expected in a Formula E motor housing?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Temperature Probe (basis.estimate_class = 4)
questions.strong_answer: Yes, the mechanical interface uses a spring-loaded retention system to maintain constant contact pressure despite high-frequency vibration.

actuation_kinematics#4.intro: Two specialists are required to validate the electromagnetic efficiency, thermal capacity, and mechanical integrity of the high-speed motor assembly.

cards.specialist_role: A senior electromagnetic machine design engineer
cards.background: Delivered high-speed permanent magnet synchronous machines for motorsport, including finite element analysis of iron losses and rotor windage at high frequencies.
cards.covers: Motor electromagnetic efficiency and thermal dissipation

questions.question: Does the electromagnetic model account for realistic iron and windage losses at nineteen thousand five hundred revolutions?
questions.grounded_in: 7-5-physics-critique.json · engineering_plausibility
questions.strong_answer: The model must show calculated losses exceeding one kilowatt, with thermal dissipation systems sized to handle the resulting heat flux.

questions.question: Must the motor electromagnetic design be scaled to support the full three hundred fifty kilowatt mechanical output?
questions.grounded_in: 7-5-physics-critique.json · brief_to_design_fidelity
questions.strong_answer: The design must demonstrate structural and thermal capability for the full three hundred fifty kilowatt peak, regardless of software limiting.

cards.background: Hands-on experience designing high-torque density motor housings, cooling jackets, and rotating assemblies for high-speed electric vehicle traction applications.
cards.typically_at: An electric vehicle powertrain equipment vendor
cards.covers: Motor structural components and cooling integration

questions.question: Is the cooling jacket geometry sufficient to manage the thermal load of a three hundred fifty kilowatt machine?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Motor Cooling Jacket
questions.strong_answer: The jacket must provide adequate surface area and coolant flow velocity to maintain stator temperatures within insulation class limits.

questions.question: Are the rotor barrel and shaft dimensions sufficient to maintain structural integrity at three hundred fifty kilowatt peak…
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Hollow Rotor Barrel
questions.strong_answer: The design must confirm that stress levels remain within fatigue limits for the specified peak torque and rotational speed.

structure_containment#5.intro: Two specialists are required to validate the structural integrity and thermal containment design of the front motor generator unit assembly.

cards.background: Delivered high-torque electric drivetrain housings and structural mounting systems for professional motorsport or high-performance electric vehicle programmes.
cards.typically_at: A high-performance electric vehicle engineering consultancy
cards.covers: Traction Drive Housing, Mounting Ear Set, Cassette Cover

questions.question: Does the Traction Drive Housing wall thickness provide sufficient stiffness to prevent bearing misalignment under peak torque?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Traction Drive Housing (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: The design must demonstrate modal frequency separation from motor excitation harmonics to ensure structural stability under maximum load.

questions.question: Are the Mounting Ear Set geometries optimised to distribute chassis-induced fatigue loads without inducing stress concentrations?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Mounting Ear Set (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: A strong answer confirms finite element analysis validation of load paths and fatigue life cycles exceeding the race season requirements.

cards.specialist_role: A senior electrical systems integration engineer
cards.background: Hands-on experience designing high-voltage shielding and thermal management enclosures for traction inverters and electric motors in racing environments.
cards.covers: Hv Shield Cover, Traction Inverter, Traction Motor, Nameplate

questions.question: Does the High Voltage Shield Cover design maintain electromagnetic compatibility compliance while allowing necessary thermal dissipation?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Hv Shield Cover (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method llm_estimate)
questions.strong_answer: The design must ensure shielding continuity across all joints while meeting thermal resistance targets for the internal power electronics.

questions.question: Is the Traction Inverter enclosure volume sufficient to accommodate the required cooling flow rates for continuous operation?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Traction Inverter (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: The answer confirms that internal fluid paths are sized to prevent pressure drops that would compromise inverter thermal performance.

safety_protection#6.intro: Two specialists are required to validate the safety protection design architecture and ensure high-voltage system integrity for the front motor generator unit.

cards.background: Delivered safety-critical inverter desaturation detection and phase overcurrent protection systems for high-performance electric vehicle powertrains.
cards.typically_at: A tier-one electric vehicle powertrain supplier
cards.covers: Inverter desaturation and phase overcurrent protection

questions.question: Does the phase overcurrent trip threshold provide sufficient margin against transient peak currents during regenerative braking?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Phase Overcurrent Trip (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: The threshold is set at 1.2 times peak current to prevent nuisance trips while protecting power semiconductors during fault conditions.

questions.question: Is the inverter desaturation protection response time fast enough to prevent catastrophic failure during a short circuit?
questions.grounded_in: state.costBasis.lines · Inverter Desat Protection (basis.rfq_recommended = true, method class_reference)
questions.strong_answer: The circuit detects desaturation within two microseconds, triggering a soft shutdown before the insulated gate bipolar transistor reaches thermal limits.

holds.required_evidence: Calibrated dyno raw data + torque/efficiency map over speed, current, voltage, and coolant conditions, revision-hashed to the assembly.
holds.measurement_recipe: Mount the revision-matched MGU and inverter on a calibrated dyno; hold coolant inlet conditions, sweep the modelled speed/current grid, and record shaft torque, DC/AC power, temperatures, and efficiency.
holds.acceptance_band: At revision-matched points, measured torque is within ±10% of the model and efficiency within ±3 percentage points, with no limit exceedance.

holds.required_evidence: Hardware-in-the-loop pass on the populated inverter revision, including safe-off, sensing, resolver, CAN, desaturation, and fault handling.
holds.measurement_recipe: Connect the populated inverter to a real-time plant simulator; replay normal, sensor-fault, resolver, CAN-loss, desaturation, and safe-off cases while logging commands, sensed values, and protection timing.
holds.acceptance_band: Every commanded state and protection transition matches the approved sequence; scaled analogue channels are within ±5% and no unsafe output persists after a trip.

holds.required_evidence: Measured pressure-flow curves for the motor jacket and inverter cold plate at controlled coolant temperature and concentration.
holds.measurement_recipe: Bench each revision-matched coolant article with the specified coolant mix and inlet temperature; step flow across the operating range and record stabilised inlet/outlet pressure, flow, and fluid temperature.
holds.acceptance_band: Measured pressure drop is within ±15% of each modelled point for both articles and preserves the predicted monotonic pressure-flow trend.

holds.required_evidence: Heater-plate test with calibrated module/case/coolant temperatures and TIM/contact stack matching the populated SiC module revision.
holds.measurement_recipe: Build the revision-matched module/TIM/cold-plate stack, apply calibrated heater power at controlled coolant conditions, and log steady module, case, plate, inlet, and outlet temperatures.
holds.acceptance_band: Steady module temperature is within ±5 °C of prediction and measured junction-to-coolant thermal resistance is within ±15% of the model.

holds.required_evidence: Instrumented overspeed/retention test and correlated rotor stress model at the controlled maximum-speed release condition.
holds.measurement_recipe: Spin the revision-matched rotor in a guarded rig through the approved speed steps; record speed, vibration, strain or growth, and post-test magnet/sleeve/bridge inspection evidence.
holds.acceptance_band: Measured strain or radial growth is within ±15% of the structural model, critical-speed trend agrees within ±10%, and retention remains intact.

holds.required_evidence: Double-pulse switching waveforms on populated SiC hardware with measured commutation-loop ESL, overshoot, switching loss, and gate settings.
holds.measurement_recipe: Run a guarded double-pulse test on the populated revision at the modelled DC bus/current points; capture gate voltage, VDS, current, timing, temperature, and commutation-loop geometry.
holds.acceptance_band: Measured loop ESL is within ±20% of prediction, voltage overshoot within ±10%, and Eon/Eoff within ±15%, with no protection or device-limit breach.

hardwareCorrelation.honesty: Software-only work can prepare model-linked bench recipes. It cannot close correlation: PASS needs revision-matched physical data. Every hold remains OPEN and ship_ok remains false.

assumptionBasedDesign.pitch: Under frozen packaging and duty assumptions consistent with the public Formula E front-kit envelope, the concentric motor–inverter–planetary–diff layout is sized into the bay. The electromagnetic duty-torque screen does not clear (mean / reliability vs required shaft torque at n_max) — peak FEMM torque alone is not a pass. Not homologated — replace assumptions when JLR inputs arrive; ship_ok stays false.
assumptionBasedDesign.honesty: RESULT_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS means educated guesses were frozen and named, then models were run. It is not hardware correlation and not ship_ok. NEEDS_PARTNER_INPUT / NEEDS_HARDWARE rows are deliberate — we did not invent them.

provenance.why: state.json carried no fpkConcentricGeometry section and no fpk_*_mm fallback quantities, so em_fia_front_kit_case raised 'Missing positive twin quantity: fpk_stator_od_mm' before solving. Every value here is what the 2026-08-02 solve RECORDED reading, so it is a recovered statement rather than a new assumption. stack_len_mm is deliberately omitted: DEC-009 adopted 130 mm and the contract holds it.

deliberately_absent.stack_len_mm: DEC-009 adopted 130 mm and the contract holds it; restoring 97.58 here would silently revert the decision

field_by_field.why_this_list_exists: The first restore on 2026-08-04 named only radial and housing dimensions. The magnet fields were omitted, fell back to solver defaults, and produced a solve of DEC-009 stack + PRE-REBALANCE magnets — 47.14 N.m for a machine nobody designed — which then cost three wrong diagnoses. Any field not named here is a default, not a neutral.
